l4_steps.name: Monitor ATPCO tax circulars and government notices
l4_steps.input: ATPCO Circular alerts, IATA Tax Monitor notifications, government tax authority bulletins
l4_steps.output: Change alert log with effective dates, affected markets, and change type classification
l4_steps.kpi: Alert intake within 2 hrs of ATPCO circular publication; 100% circular coverage
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Tax Information System does not auto-push alerts to the PSS — manual monitoring is required, creating risk of missed effective dates on government-mandated tax changes

l4_steps.name: Classify surcharge/tax change type and geographic scope
l4_steps.output: Classified change record: government tax (TC3), fuel surcharge YQ (TC35), carrier surcharge YR (TC36), or airport levy
l4_steps.kpi: Classification accuracy ≥99%; misclassification rate <1 per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: YQ vs. YR distinction is frequently misclassified under IATA Resolution 728, triggering incorrect tax calculation in Amadeus Altéa PSS and downstream GDS fare builds

l4_steps.name: Assess effective date urgency and regulatory deadline
l4_steps.input: Classified change record, regulatory effective date
l4_steps.output: Filing priority flag: emergency (<24 hrs), standard (3–7 days), or scheduled (>7 days)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of government-mandated tax changes filed before regulatory effective date; zero late filings
l4_steps.pain_point: Government tax changes in high-growth markets (e.g., APAC airport levies, EU ETS surcharges) often arrive with <48 hrs notice, requiring emergency ATPCO filing protocols that bypass the standard 3-day review cycle

l4_steps.name: Model fuel surcharge (YQ) rates by sector distance band
l4_steps.input: Jet fuel price index (IATA Fuel Monitor), sector distance bands, current YQ rate table
l4_steps.output: Proposed YQ rate schedule by sector range (short/medium/long-haul) and cabin class
l4_steps.kpi: YQ cost recovery rate ≥95% of actual fuel surcharge exposure per sector
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel price volatility (±15% intra-quarter) makes static YQ tables misaligned with actual cost within weeks of filing; PROS RM lacks native YQ recalculation — analysts must run Excel models outside the system

l4_steps.name: Calculate carrier-imposed surcharge (YR) per market and cabin
l4_steps.input: Operating cost variance report, competitor YR benchmarks from ATPCO Airfare Insight
l4_steps.output: Proposed YR rate schedule by market pair, cabin class, and booking class
l4_steps.kpi: YR revenue contribution maintains ≥8% of total ticket revenue per long-haul market
l4_steps.pain_point: YR surcharges are commercially discretionary but are often misread by consumers as government taxes, generating EU Regulation 1008/2008 fare transparency complaints and compliance team workload

l4_steps.name: Benchmark proposed rates against ATPCO peer submissions
l4_steps.input: Proposed YQ/YR rate schedule, competitor published rates from ATPCO database
l4_steps.output: Benchmark comparison report: proposed rate vs. market range (min/median/max per sector)
l4_steps.kpi: Proposed rates within ±10% of market median for ≥90% of benchmarked sectors
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Airfare Insight competitor data lags 24–48 hrs, so benchmarking is retrospective; carriers can undercut within hours of filing, invalidating the benchmark before the rate is published

l4_steps.name: Obtain VP Pricing and revenue management sign-off
l4_steps.input: Benchmark comparison report, finance impact analysis, fuel cost exposure data
l4_steps.output: Approved surcharge rate schedule with authorisation record and timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Sign-off cycle time <24 hrs for standard changes; <4 hrs for emergency filings
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP Finance approval workflows are not integrated with ATPCO filing system — approval is documented in SAP but filing is manual in ATPCO, creating audit gaps when approval and filing timestamps differ

l4_steps.name: Configure government tax codes in ATPCO Tax Engine (TC3)
l4_steps.input: Approved tax change record, regulatory bulletin, affected market list
l4_steps.output: ATPCO TC3 tax records configured for correct tax code, rate, currency, and effective date
l4_steps.kpi: TC3 record accuracy rate ≥99.9%; zero miscoded tax records in quarterly ATPCO audit
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO TC3 configuration for multi-tier tax structures (e.g., UK APD bands A/B, US segment fees + PFC + TSA) requires manual entry of up to 12 sub-records per market — high error risk with no built-in field validation in the ATPCO UI

l4_steps.name: File YQ/YR surcharge records to ATPCO (TC35/TC36)
l4_steps.input: Approved YQ/YR rate schedule, effective and discontinue dates, geographic scope
l4_steps.output: ATPCO TC35 (YQ) and TC36 (YR) records submitted with ATPCO confirmation reference
l4_steps.kpi: Filing submission within 2 hrs of sign-off approval; 100% of records submitted before effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO TC35/TC36 records do not support conditional logic (e.g., 'YQ applies only if fuel index exceeds threshold') — dynamic fuel surcharges must be manually re-filed each time the fuel index crosses a rate band boundary

l4_steps.name: Validate ATPCO filing acceptance and record integrity
l4_steps.input: ATPCO submission confirmation, filing reference number
l4_steps.output: Validation report: all records accepted, no rejection codes, effective dates confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Filing rejection rate <0.5%; all rejections resolved and resubmitted within 1 hr
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO validation errors are returned as cryptic rejection codes requiring specialist knowledge to decode; documentation is maintained in offline PDFs not integrated with the filing UI, causing an average 45-minute resolution time per error

l4_steps.name: Monitor GDS pick-up and cross-channel distribution lag
l4_steps.input: ATPCO filing confirmation, effective date/time, GDS polling schedule
l4_steps.output: GDS pick-up confirmation for Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS; distribution lag report
l4_steps.kpi: GDS distribution lag ≤4 hrs post ATPCO effective time for all three major GDS channels
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS poll ATPCO on different schedules (Sabre hourly, Travelport 2-hourly, Amadeus 4-hourly), creating distribution windows where channels display different total tax amounts — generating fare integrity complaints from OTAs and TMCs

l4_steps.name: Update surcharge and tax tables in Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO filing confirmation, GDS distribution confirmation, approved rate schedule
l4_steps.output: Altéa PSS surcharge and tax tables updated; configuration change log created
l4_steps.kpi: Altéa configuration update completed within 2 hrs of ATPCO effective time; zero stale rate records in PSS
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS tax table updates are a manual configuration task — there is no automated sync from ATPCO filings to Altéa, requiring a separate maintenance window that can drift from GDS distribution timing and create channel pricing inconsistencies

l4_steps.name: Update NDC API gateway tax calculation rules
l4_steps.input: Approved rate schedule, Altéa PSS configuration update confirmation
l4_steps.output: NDC API tax rules updated; API response test package generated
l4_steps.kpi: NDC API tax calculation matches ATPCO reference for 100% of test fare builds
l4_steps.pain_point: The NDC API gateway tax calculation is a separate microservice from Altéa PSS — version mismatches between PSS tax tables and NDC API rules produce pricing inconsistencies between indirect (GDS) and direct (NDC) channels, violating IATA NDC Standard Level 4 fare transparency requirements

l4_steps.name: Execute end-to-end fare build test across all channels
l4_steps.input: Test itinerary set (20 representative market pairs), ATPCO reference tax/surcharge totals
l4_steps.output: Channel test report: fare total vs. reference for GDS, NDC, and IBE channels
l4_steps.kpi: Test pass rate 100% across all 20 itineraries on first run; zero price discrepancies exceeding €0.01
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Selling Platform test environment uses a 6-hr delayed ATPCO snapshot — post-filing tests on live-equivalent data require production credentials, increasing configuration change risk during the testing window

l4_steps.name: Audit post-effective-date fare calculations via ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Live sold-fare sample (T+1 day), ATPCO reference tax and surcharge records
l4_steps.output: Audit report: percentage of sold fares with correct surcharge and tax applied by market and channel
l4_steps.kpi: Surcharge accuracy on sold fares ≥99.5% within 24 hrs of effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Airfare Insight audit is sample-based, not exhaustive — systematic miscalculation on low-volume markets can persist for weeks before appearing in the sample, leading to under-collection risk and potential regulatory penalties

l4_steps.name: Reconcile BSP/ARC settlement data against surcharge revenue
l4_steps.input: BSP/ARC settlement reports, ATPCO-expected surcharge revenue by market
l4_steps.output: Surcharge revenue reconciliation report: collected vs. expected, variance by market and channel
l4_steps.kpi: Surcharge revenue variance <1% of expected monthly collection; reconciliation completed within T+5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP settlement data does not tag YQ and YR separately from base fare in all markets — revenue accounting must manually decompose settlement records, a process requiring 3–4 hrs per settlement cycle and prone to allocation errors

l4_steps.name: Investigate variance and initiate corrective ATPCO filing or ADM
l4_steps.input: Surcharge reconciliation report, variance-flagged markets and booking references
l4_steps.output: Root cause analysis, corrective ATPCO filing or PSS configuration patch, variance closure report
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue variance >1% resolved and corrected within 5 business days; zero repeat variances for same market within 90-day window
l4_steps.pain_point: Corrective ATPCO filings for past-ticketed fares require manual Agency Debit Memo (ADM) issuance via BSP/ARC for each affected booking — ADM processing cost can exceed the surcharge variance value for low-value corrections, forcing a commercial write-off vs. regulatory recovery trade-off
